chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Whatever condition existed before the marriage, the marriage nullifies it, and whatever exists after the marriage is valid."
And he said: "If the period is specified, it is Mut'ah (temporary marriage), and if the period is not specified, it is a permanent marriage."
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Mut'ah and permanent marriage in Shia jurisprudence regarding time stipulation?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal hierarchy of stipulations in marriage, establishing that pre-contractual conditions are subsumed by the marriage act, whereas post-contractual ones remain binding. He further provides a critical jurisprudential criterion for distinguishing between *Mut'ah* (temporary marriage) and *Nikah al-Mutlaq* (permanent marriage) based on the explicit stipulation of a time limit, a key point of contention between Shia and Sunni schools. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia marriage law in accommodating specific contractual terms while maintaining the integrity of the marital bond.
